title: Diocletian retires to his palace
description: The emperor Diocletian abdicates and moves to the fortified palace built for him on the Dalmatian coast, around which the city of Split later grows.

title: Pope recognises Duke Branimir
description: Pope John VIII blesses Branimir and his people, treating Croatia as a state independent of both the Franks and Byzantium.

title: Tomislav named king
description: A papal letter connected with the church council of Split addresses Tomislav as king, the basis for dating the Croatian kingdom from this year.

title: Coronation of Zvonimir
description: Demetrius Zvonimir is crowned by a legate of Pope Gregory VII and swears loyalty to the papacy.

title: Coloman of Hungary crowned king of Croatia
description: The Hungarian king is crowned at Biograd, beginning a union of the Croatian and Hungarian crowns that lasts until 1918.

title: Siege of Zara
description: The Fourth Crusade takes and sacks the Christian city of Zadar for Venice in payment for its fleet.

title: Golden Bull of Zagreb
description: After the Mongol invasion King Béla IV makes Gradec a free royal city, the founding charter of Zagreb.

title: Treaty of Zadar
description: Venice gives up Dalmatia to Louis I of Hungary, and Dubrovnik becomes in practice a self-governing republic.

title: Dalmatia sold to Venice
description: Ladislaus of Naples sells his rights to Dalmatia to Venice for 100,000 ducats, and the coast stays Venetian until 1797.

title: Battle of Krbava Field
description: An Ottoman force returning from a raid destroys the army of the Croatian nobility.

title: Election in Cetin
description: After the death of Louis II at Mohács the Croatian nobles choose Ferdinand of Habsburg as king, beginning nearly four centuries of Habsburg rule.

title: Peasant revolt of Matija Gubec
description: A revolt of Croatian and Slovene serfs against their lords is defeated at Stubica and its leader is executed in Zagreb.

title: Battle of Sisak
description: Croatian and Habsburg troops defeat the army of the Ottoman governor of Bosnia, halting the Ottoman advance into Croatia.

title: Dubrovnik earthquake
description: An earthquake destroys most of the city and kills several thousand people, a blow from which the republic's trade never fully recovers.

title: Execution of Zrinski and Frankopan
description: Petar Zrinski and Fran Krsto Frankopan are beheaded for conspiring against Emperor Leopold I, and the estates of the two leading Croatian noble families are confiscated.

title: End of the Republic of Ragusa
description: The French, who had occupied Dubrovnik in 1806, abolish the republic, ending more than four centuries of independence.

title: Jelačić abolishes serfdom
description: The newly appointed ban Josip Jelačić proclaims the end of serfdom in Croatia, and later in the year leads an army against the Hungarian revolution.

title: Croatian–Hungarian Settlement
description: An agreement gives Croatia-Slavonia its own parliament, government and official language within the Hungarian half of the Dual Monarchy.

title: Sabor breaks with Austria-Hungary
polity: State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs
description: The Croatian parliament ends all ties with Austria and Hungary and joins the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, which unites with Serbia five weeks later.

title: Stjepan Radić shot in parliament
polity: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes
description: A Montenegrin Serb deputy shoots the leader of the Croatian Peasant Party and four colleagues on the floor of the assembly, and the king imposes a dictatorship months later.

title: Cvetković–Maček Agreement
description: The Yugoslav government and the Croatian Peasant Party agree to create a self-governing Banovina of Croatia.

title: Independent State of Croatia proclaimed
description: As German troops enter Zagreb the Ustaše declare a state under Ante Pavelić, which persecutes and kills Serbs, Jews and Roma.

title: Jasenovac concentration camp
description: The Ustaše regime runs its largest camp complex, where an estimated 80,000 to 100,000 Serbs, Roma, Jews and political opponents are killed.

title: First session of ZAVNOH
description: The Partisan-led anti-fascist council of Croatia meets for the first time, the body from which the post-war Croatian republic is formed.

title: Bleiburg repatriations
description: British forces turn back soldiers of the Independent State of Croatia and civilians fleeing with them, and tens of thousands are killed by the Partisans on forced marches.

title: Croatian Spring suppressed
description: Tito forces the reformist leadership of the Croatian communists to resign, ending a movement for greater economic and cultural autonomy.

title: First multi-party elections
description: The Croatian Democratic Union of Franjo Tuđman wins the first free elections since the Second World War.

title: Independence declared
description: The Croatian parliament declares independence from Yugoslavia on the same day as Slovenia, and war with the Yugoslav army and Serb forces follows.

title: Fall of Vukovar
description: After an 87-day siege that leaves the town in ruins, Vukovar falls to the Yugoslav army and Serb paramilitaries, who then kill about 200 prisoners at Ovčara.

title: Operation Storm
description: The Croatian army retakes the self-proclaimed Republic of Serbian Krajina in four days, ending the war in Croatia, and most of the region's Serbs flee.

title: Croatia joins the European Union
description: Croatia becomes the 28th member of the European Union, four years after joining NATO.
